title: Subsystem
description: A GM Core-style victory-point subsystem instance (Victory Points, Influence, Research, Chases, Infiltration, Hacking, or a custom homebrew one). One or more point pools, built from discrete obstacles/checks whose degrees of success move those pools, bounded by a round/time/attempt limit, resolving to a win/lose/graduated state. Grounded in GM Core Ch.4 (reference/srd/gm-core/1125-1170). The six named subsystems share this core shape but diverge in real ways (see subsystemSpecific) — don't force a Hacking or Infiltration instance to pretend it's a simple point pool if it isn't one.

description.description: Narrative framing — what winning/losing this subsystem means in-fiction.

scale.description: GM Core's own reference scale for sizing point targets: quick encounter ~3-5 pts; long encounter ~7-10 (threshold 4); most of a session ~15-25 (thresholds 5/10/15); adventure-wide sideline ~15-20; adventure-wide forefront ~25-50 (thresholds 10/20/30/40).

pools.description: Usually one pool (e.g. Victory Points). Multiple for the 'Multiple Point' VP variant (e.g. PCs' points vs. a rival's, both racing to a target) or Infiltration's IP/AP/EP split.

mode.description: Accumulating = race up to a win target. Diminishing = protect the pool from hitting a loss floor.

owner.description: VP's 'Enemy Victory Points' variant: a pool driven entirely by PC actions but tracking the OPPOSITION's progress, sometimes inverted (a PC crit success reduces it).

thresholds.description: Graduated mid-run benefits/complications as this pool crosses a value, not just a single win/lose at the end. GM Core warns over-succeeding can have negative narrative consequences too — thresholds aren't guaranteed to be monotonically good.

objectives.description: Infiltration's goal layer above obstacles: a broad aim requiring a chosen subset of obstacles cleared. Leave empty for subsystems without this hierarchy (most of them).

requiredObstacleCount.description: How many of obstacleRefs must be cleared, not necessarily all of them.

sequential.description: Whether this objective must be completed before the next one unlocks.

obstacles.description: The discrete tasks/checks that make up this subsystem. May legitimately be EMPTY since `spends` exists: a subsystem whose whole job is to be a visible clock the players spend down by choosing things has real pools, real thresholds and no DC'd task anywhere in it. Still required to be present, so that an authoring slip reads as "no obstacles here" rather than as a forgotten field.

poolEffects.description: Point deltas per degree of success, sparse — omit a degree that has no effect. Most subsystems here only ever specify 3 of the 4 degrees (crit success/success/crit failure), leaving plain failure as +0 by omission.

dcModifierEffect.description: Hacking's vulnerability pattern: succeeding at this obstacle doesn't award points, it permanently lowers another obstacle's DC instead.

maxYield.description: Research's per-check point cap: this obstacle can't contribute more than this many points total, however many times it's attempted.

scope.description: Infiltration: individual = each PC earns their own progress and can only overcome it once per PC; group = the party pools progress and can only overcome it once for the whole party.

persistent.description: Hacking countermeasure-style: auto-retriggers every round until disabled, rather than being a one-time obstacle.

optional.description: Infiltration's Opportunities: doesn't count toward objectives/progress, grants a side benefit instead.

spends.description: Authored, check-free ways to move a pool. Every `obstacle` is a DC'd check; a spend is the other half — a flat, GM-adjudicated cost for something a player simply chooses to do. Written for the scene-runner's visible clocks (design/theatre-of-the-mind-staging.md, ux-doctrine.md §3): a shift's twelve walls is a diminishing pool, and 'mapping the tag distribution costs two of them' is a spend. Cost is authored because the GM prices the action, not the dice.

label.description: What the players are choosing to do, in their words — "Map the tag distribution", "Interview a shopkeeper properly".

poolRef.description: id of the pool in this subsystem's `pools` that this moves.

delta.description: Signed, and applied as-is: negative spends a diminishing pool down, positive can give time back. Never assume the sign from the pool's mode.

note.description: GM-facing colour on what this costs or buys.

complications.description: Infiltration-style forced extra obstacles triggered by a crit failure, a threshold, or GM/story need. Must be resolved before other progress continues.

eligibility.description: Usually "any PC may attempt any obstacle they can justify."

actionsPerRound.default: one action toward the subsystem per PC per round

mandatoryParticipation.description: Chases: a PC who doesn't/can't act on their turn costs the party a point automatically.

bounding.description: What limits the whole subsystem, since every one of these is bounded by something different.

dynamicAdjustment.description: GM Core flags that a specific in-fiction choice can shrink/extend the bound mid-scene — note that here if relevant, rather than assuming the bound is fixed once play starts.

loseCondition.description: Research and Hacking, per the source text, don't state a hard loss condition — they're bounded by escalating risk/time instead. Leave null rather than forcing one.

subsystemSpecific.description: Bespoke fields that don't generalize across all six named subsystems — don't force-fit these into the shape above. Examples: Influence's NPC-level Resistances/Weaknesses (DC modifiers keyed to narrative topics) and Discover action (reveals hidden obstacle parameters instead of moving a pool); Chases' named sub-type (Chase Down/Run Away/Beat the Clock/Competitive) and per-obstacle point reset (no carryover between obstacles); Infiltration's Edge Points (a banked, pre-earned resource from downtime Preparation activities, spent to convert a failure into a success); Hacking's simple-vs-complex mode split.

rewards.description: GM Core: reward scope tracks subsystem scope — a single-sitting subsystem usually earns accomplishment XP, multi-session earns milestone XP, low-profile tracking may earn none.
